metadata.title: Rego Policy Libraries — eo_14028 (Executive Order 14028 (May 12, 2021) — Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity: agency and supplier directives)

groups.title: Executive Order 14028 (May 12, 2021) — Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity: agency and supplier directives

controls.title: service providers collect and preserve data, information, and reporting relevant to cybersecurity event prevention, detection, response, and investigation on all information systems over which they ha

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: service providers collect and preserve data, information, and reporting relevant to cybersecurity event prevention, detection, response, and investigation on all information systems over which they have control, including systems operated on behalf of agencies, consistent with agencies' requirements

controls.title: service providers share such data, information, and reporting, as they relate to cyber incidents or potential incidents relevant to any agency with which they have contracted, directly with such agenc

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: service providers share such data, information, and reporting, as they relate to cyber incidents or potential incidents relevant to any agency with which they have contracted, directly with such agency and any other agency that the Director of OMB ... deems appropriate

controls.title: service providers collaborate with Federal cybersecurity or investigative agencies in their investigations of and responses to incidents or potential incidents on Federal Information Systems, includin

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: service providers collaborate with Federal cybersecurity or investigative agencies in their investigations of and responses to incidents or potential incidents on Federal Information Systems, including by implementing technical capabilities, such as monitoring networks for threats in collaboration with agencies they support, as needed

controls.title: service providers share cyber threat and incident information with agencies, doing so, where possible, in industry-recognized formats for incident response and remediation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: service providers share cyber threat and incident information with agencies, doing so, where possible, in industry-recognized formats for incident response and remediation

controls.title: information and communications technology (ICT) service providers entering into contracts with agencies must promptly report to such agencies when they discover a cyber incident involving a software p

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: information and communications technology (ICT) service providers entering into contracts with agencies must promptly report to such agencies when they discover a cyber incident involving a software product or service provided to such agencies or involving a support system for a software product or service provided to such agencies

controls.title: ICT service providers must also directly report to CISA whenever they report under subsection (f)(i) of this section to Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) Agencies

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: ICT service providers must also directly report to CISA whenever they report under subsection (f)(i) of this section to Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) Agencies

controls.title: Following any updates to the FAR made by the FAR Council ..., agencies shall update their agency-specific cybersecurity requirements to remove any requirements that are duplicative of such FAR updates

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Following any updates to the FAR made by the FAR Council ..., agencies shall update their agency-specific cybersecurity requirements to remove any requirements that are duplicative of such FAR updates

controls.title: Within 60 days of the date of this order, the head of each agency shall update existing agency plans to prioritize resources for the adoption and use of cloud technology as outlined in relevant OMB gu

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Within 60 days of the date of this order, the head of each agency shall update existing agency plans to prioritize resources for the adoption and use of cloud technology as outlined in relevant OMB guidance

controls.title: Within 60 days of the date of this order, the head of each agency shall develop a plan to implement Zero Trust Architecture, which shall incorporate, as appropriate, the migration steps that NIST has

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Within 60 days of the date of this order, the head of each agency shall develop a plan to implement Zero Trust Architecture, which shall incorporate, as appropriate, the migration steps that NIST has outlined in standards and guidance, describe any such steps that have already been completed, identify activities that will have the most immediate security impact, and include a schedule to implement them

controls.title: Within 60 days of the date of this order, the head of each agency shall provide a report to the Director of OMB and the APNSA discussing the plans required pursuant to subsection (b)(i) and (ii)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Within 60 days of the date of this order, the head of each agency shall provide a report to the Director of OMB and the APNSA discussing the plans required pursuant to subsection (b)(i) and (ii)

controls.title: As agencies continue to use cloud technology, they shall do so in a coordinated, deliberate way that allows the Federal Government to prevent, detect, assess, and remediate cyber incidents ... the mig

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: As agencies continue to use cloud technology, they shall do so in a coordinated, deliberate way that allows the Federal Government to prevent, detect, assess, and remediate cyber incidents ... the migration to cloud technology shall adopt Zero Trust Architecture, as practicable

controls.title: Within 90 days of the date of this order, the heads of FCEB Agencies ... shall evaluate the types and sensitivity of their respective agency's unclassified data, and shall provide to the Secretary of

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Within 90 days of the date of this order, the heads of FCEB Agencies ... shall evaluate the types and sensitivity of their respective agency's unclassified data, and shall provide to the Secretary of Homeland Security through the Director of CISA and to the Director of OMB a report based on such evaluation

controls.title: Within 180 days of the date of this order, agencies shall adopt multi-factor authentication and encryption for data at rest and in transit, to the maximum extent consistent with Federal records laws a

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Within 180 days of the date of this order, agencies shall adopt multi-factor authentication and encryption for data at rest and in transit, to the maximum extent consistent with Federal records laws and other applicable laws

controls.title: Heads of FCEB Agencies shall provide reports to the Secretary of Homeland Security through the Director of CISA, the Director of OMB, and the APNSA on their respective agency's progress in adopting mu

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Heads of FCEB Agencies shall provide reports to the Secretary of Homeland Security through the Director of CISA, the Director of OMB, and the APNSA on their respective agency's progress in adopting multifactor authentication and encryption of data at rest and in transit ... every 60 days after the date of this order until the agency has fully adopted, agency-wide, multi-factor authentication and data encryption

controls.title: Heads of FCEB Agencies that are unable to fully adopt multi-factor authentication and data encryption within 180 days of the date of this order shall, at the end of the 180-day period, provide a writt

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Heads of FCEB Agencies that are unable to fully adopt multi-factor authentication and data encryption within 180 days of the date of this order shall, at the end of the 180-day period, provide a written rationale to the Secretary of Homeland Security through the Director of CISA, the Director of OMB, and the APNSA

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: providing, when requested by a purchaser, artifacts of the execution of the tools and processes described in subsection (e)(iii) and (iv), and making publicly available summary information on completion of these actions, to include a summary description of the risks assessed and mitigated

controls.title: maintaining accurate and up-to-date data, provenance (i.e., origin) of software code or components, and controls on internal and third-party software components, tools, and services present in softwar

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: maintaining accurate and up-to-date data, provenance (i.e., origin) of software code or components, and controls on internal and third-party software components, tools, and services present in software development processes, and performing audits and enforcement of these controls on a recurring basis

controls.title: the Director of OMB ... shall take appropriate steps to require that agencies comply with such guidance [security measures for critical software under 4(i): least privilege, network segmentation, and

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: the Director of OMB ... shall take appropriate steps to require that agencies comply with such guidance [security measures for critical software under 4(i): least privilege, network segmentation, and proper configuration]

controls.title: the Director of OMB ... shall take appropriate steps to require that agencies comply with such guidelines [4(e)] with respect to software procured after the date of this order

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: the Director of OMB ... shall take appropriate steps to require that agencies comply with such guidelines [4(e)] with respect to software procured after the date of this order

controls.title: Following the issuance of any final rule amending the FAR as described in subsection (o), agencies shall, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, remove software products that do not meet t

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Following the issuance of any final rule amending the FAR as described in subsection (o), agencies shall, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, remove software products that do not meet the requirements of the amended FAR from all indefinite delivery indefinite quantity contracts; Federal Supply Schedules; Federal Government-wide Acquisition Contracts; Blanket Purchase Agreements; and Multiple Award Contracts

controls.title: agencies employing software developed and procured prior to the date of this order (legacy software) either to comply with any requirements issued pursuant to subsection (k) or to provide a plan outli

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: agencies employing software developed and procured prior to the date of this order (legacy software) either to comply with any requirements issued pursuant to subsection (k) or to provide a plan outlining actions to remediate or meet those requirements, and ... agencies seeking renewals of software contracts, including legacy software, to comply ... unless an extension or waiver is granted in accordance with subsection (l) or (m)

controls.title: The playbook shall ... be used by FCEB Agencies

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The playbook shall ... be used by FCEB Agencies

controls.title: Agencies with cybersecurity vulnerability or incident response procedures that deviate from the playbook may use such procedures only after consulting with the Director of OMB and the APNSA and demons

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Agencies with cybersecurity vulnerability or incident response procedures that deviate from the playbook may use such procedures only after consulting with the Director of OMB and the APNSA and demonstrating that these procedures meet or exceed the standards proposed in the playbook

controls.title: FCEB Agencies shall deploy an Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) initiative to support proactive detection of cybersecurity incidents within Federal Government infrastructure, active cyber hunting,

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: FCEB Agencies shall deploy an Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) initiative to support proactive detection of cybersecurity incidents within Federal Government infrastructure, active cyber hunting, containment and remediation, and incident response

controls.title: the Director of OMB ... shall issue requirements for FCEB Agencies to adopt Federal Government-wide EDR approaches. Those requirements shall support a capability of the Secretary of Homeland Security,

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: the Director of OMB ... shall issue requirements for FCEB Agencies to adopt Federal Government-wide EDR approaches. Those requirements shall support a capability of the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of CISA, to engage in cyber hunt, detection, and response activities

controls.title: Within 75 days of the date of this order, agencies shall establish or update Memoranda of Agreement (MOA) with CISA for the Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation Program to ensure object level data, a

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Within 75 days of the date of this order, agencies shall establish or update Memoranda of Agreement (MOA) with CISA for the Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation Program to ensure object level data, as defined in the MOA, are available and accessible to CISA, consistent with applicable law

controls.title: It is essential that agencies and their IT service providers collect and maintain such data [network and system logs on Federal Information Systems] and, when necessary to address a cyber incident on

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is essential that agencies and their IT service providers collect and maintain such data [network and system logs on Federal Information Systems] and, when necessary to address a cyber incident on FCEB Information Systems, provide them upon request to the Secretary of Homeland Security through the Director of CISA and to the FBI, consistent with applicable law

controls.title: Logs shall be protected by cryptographic methods to ensure integrity once collected and periodically verified against the hashes throughout their retention. Data shall be retained in a manner consiste

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Logs shall be protected by cryptographic methods to ensure integrity once collected and periodically verified against the hashes throughout their retention. Data shall be retained in a manner consistent with all applicable privacy laws and regulations

controls.title: policies for agencies to establish requirements for logging, log retention, and log management, which shall ensure centralized access and visibility for the highest level security operations center of

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: policies for agencies to establish requirements for logging, log retention, and log management, which shall ensure centralized access and visibility for the highest level security operations center of each agency

controls.title: requirements to ensure that, upon request, agencies provide logs to the Secretary of Homeland Security through the Director of CISA and to the FBI, consistent with applicable law

parts.prose: requirements to ensure that, upon request, agencies provide logs to the Secretary of Homeland Security through the Director of CISA and to the FBI, consistent with applicable law
